plain.text: When Jacob learned there was grain in Egypt, he sent ten of his sons to buy some, but kept Benjamin at home in case harm came to him. Joseph, as governor, sold grain to everyone. His brothers came and bowed down to him with their faces to the ground. Joseph recognised them, but they did not recognise him. He remembered his dreams. He spoke harshly and accused them of being spies. They said they were twelve brothers, sons of one man; the youngest was at home and one was no more. Joseph put them in prison for three days, then said one would stay while the others took grain home and brought back their youngest brother. They said to one another, "Surely we are being punished because of our brother. We saw how distressed he was when he pleaded with us, but we would not listen." They did not realise Joseph understood them. He turned away and wept. Then he had Simeon tied up before their eyes.

Joseph secretly had their silver returned in their sacks. On the way, one found his silver, and their hearts sank: "What is this that God has done to us?" At home they told Jacob everything, and all found their silver, which frightened them. Jacob said, "You have deprived me of my children. Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more, and now you want to take Benjamin. Everything is against me!" Reuben offered his own two sons as a guarantee, but Jacob refused to let Benjamin go: "If harm comes to him, you will bring my grey head down to the grave in sorrow."

summary.bigIdea: Joseph's brothers come to Egypt and bow to him without knowing him, and their guilt over Joseph surfaces.
points: The brothers bow down to Joseph, just as he dreamed.
Joseph tests them, and they admit their guilt about what they did to him.
Joseph weeps in secret; Jacob refuses to risk losing Benjamin.
summary.reflection: The brothers' old guilt came back years later. Is there something from the past you need to bring to God?
